fullPassage: Why do humans have the counterproductive instinct to favor natural products in the absence of knowledge of their benefits or their potential for harm? The answer likely lies in our genes. Our species, through most of its evolutionary history, relied heavily upon experience to judge whether ingestion of something was beneficial (i.e., nutritional or medicinal) versus whether it was dangerous (i.e., poisonous). We evolved the instinct to avoid plants that made us sick and favored those that made us well. Treating unknowns with great caution provided a terrific survival advantage. Today, we trust that products of nature are safe to consume. But those pills coming off a pharmaceutical production line look nothing like what our instincts tell us is safe to eat. The ingredients remind us of a high school chemistry lab. Yet we are expected to consume them. Thus, we treat them with favor just as our distant ancestors regarded a new plant. When in need of a remedy, we are drawn to derivatives of our food, plant products, which we perceive to be safe, and not artificial products of science.

❌ ① whether: 'to judge whether ingestion of something was beneficial... versus whether it was dangerous' — whether A versus whether B 병렬구조. '~인지 아닌지 판단하다' 정상

✅ ④ being: 'which we perceive being safe' — perceive + 목적어 + to be + 형용사 구문이 정확. 'which we perceive to be safe'가 맞음. being은 perceive의 목적보어 형태로 부적절 ← 정답
det.tip: perceive + O + to be: 5형식 지각동사 구문. see/find/consider/perceive + 목적어 + to be + 보어. being은 진행형 느낌으로 부적절

인류는 진화 역사에서 경험에 크게 의존하여 섭취 여부를 판단했다.
오늘날 사람들은 자연 제품이 안전하다고 신뢰하는 경향이 있다.
제약 생산라인의 약품은 본능적으로 안전해 보인다.

questions.passage: Why do humans have the counterproductive instinct to favor natural products in the absence of knowledge of their benefits or their potential for harm? The answer likely lies in our genes. Our species, through most of its evolutionary history, relied heavily upon experience to judge whether ingestion of something was beneficial (i.e., nutritional or medicinal) versus whether it was dangerous (i.e., poisonous). We evolved the instinct to avoid plants that made us sick and favored those that made us well. Treating unknowns with great caution provided a terrific survival advantage. Today, we trust that products of nature are safe to consume. But those pills coming off a pharmaceutical production line look nothing like what our instincts tell us is safe to eat. The ingredients remind us of a high school chemistry lab. Yet we are expected to consume them. Thus, we treat them with favor just as our distant ancestors regarded a new plant. When in need of a remedy, we are drawn to derivatives of our food, plant products, which we perceive to be safe, and not artificial products of science.
questions.stem:
다음 글을 읽고, 인류가 진화 역사에서 무언가를 섭취하는 것이 유익한지 위험한지 판단하기 위해 크게 의존한 것을 본문에서 찾아 영어로 쓰시오. (영어로, 7단어)

[힌트] '경험에 크게 의존하여 판단하다'라는 의미이다.

det.korean: 경험에 크게 의존하여 판단: relied heavily upon experience to judge
det.analysis:
'Our species, through most of its evolutionary history, relied heavily upon experience to judge whether ingestion of something was beneficial... versus whether it was dangerous...' — 진화 역사에서 무언가를 섭취하는 것이 유익한지 위험한지 판단하기 위해 '경험에 크게 의존했다'.

relied(과거동사) + heavily(부사) + upon(전치사) + experience(명사) + to(전치사) + judge(동사원형) = 7단어 (relied heavily upon experience to judge 중 'whether...'는 judge의 목적절)
det.tip: 본문 위치: 세 번째 문장. relied heavily upon experience = 경험에 크게 의존했다. to judge = 판단하기 위해

questions.stem:
다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말을 아래 조건에 맞게 영어로 쓰시오.
[조건] (1) drawn, to, derivatives, of, our, food를 모두 사용할 것
(2) 정확히 6단어로 쓸 것

det.korean: 치료제가 필요할 때 음식의 파생물에 이끌린다
det.analysis:
'When in need of a remedy, we are drawn to derivatives of our food, plant products...' — be drawn to = ~에 이끌리다. derivatives of our food = 음식의 파생물. 인간이 약품 대신 자연 식품 유래 제품에 이끌린다는 글의 결론부.

구문 분석: drawn(과거분사/수동) + to(전치사) + derivatives(명사) + of(전치사) + our(소유격) + food(명사) = 6단어
det.tip: be drawn to = ~에 이끌리다 (수동태). derivatives = 파생물. 조건 6단어 = wa 6단어 일치
